claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - Alex. He's 18 now, but he's still in college doing his A-levels, so I was wondering if I can still claim for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Alex being 18 and doing A-levels is relevant to eligibility.

Let me ask you a few more questions to assess your situation:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex:

**Does Alex live with you, or if not, do you contribute financially towards his upkeep (such as for food, clothes, pocket money, etc.)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me anymore - he lives with his dad. But I do still help out financially. I contribute towards his expenses - you know, helping with clothes, his travel costs for college, things like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for explaining that. To help determine your eligibility, I need to understand more about your financial contributions:

**How much do you contribute towards Alex's expenses, and how often do you make these contributions (weekly, monthly, or as a lump sum)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I give about £26 a week - so just over a hundred pounds a month. I try to send it weekly to help with his day-to-day costs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that detail. That's helpful information.

One more important question:

**Is Alex's dad (or anyone else) currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, his dad isn't claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just something we never sorted out properly when Alex moved in with him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

✓ **Age and Education**: Even though Alex is 18, Child Benefit can continue for young people under 20 who are in approved education or training. His A-level studies at college count as approved education.

✓ **Responsibility for the child**: Although Alex doesn't live with you, you're still considered responsible for him because you're contributing £26 per week towards his upkeep (for clothes, travel costs, etc.). This amount meets the requirement of contributing at least as much as the Child Benefit payment itself.

✓ **UK residence**: You live in the UK (Manchester).

✓ **No duplicate claims**: Alex's dad isn't currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, and only one person can claim for each child.

**Next steps**: You can make a claim for Child Benefit for Alex. Just be aware that if you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about claiming Child Benefit?
